packageRules.description: Minor, patch, pin and digest automerge once CI is green, straight to the base branch with no PR (automergeType: branch above). The gate is minimumReleaseAge plus a passing test run on the renovate/ branch, so the repo's CI has to run on push to renovate/**. A red run, or checks still pending after prNotPendingHours (25), makes Renovate open a PR instead, so a PR always means a human is needed. A repo with no CI at all has to set ignoreTests: true for itself, because a branch with no status check and no check run resolves to yellow and would only ever surface as a PR after 25 hours.

A major is never automerged, in any manager or repo, so it is the one update type that always gets a PR. It requests a review, and that request is the notification that one is waiting. Majors are where upstream notes change what you do, so they stay a decision.

GitHub Actions bump at every update type, major included, so this rule sits after the major rule above and wins for the github-actions manager. A workflow action is not a running service: it cannot reach a cluster, it has no data to migrate, and the blast radius of a bad one is a red CI run on the PR that introduced it, which is the thing that blocks the merge in the first place. Treating a major here as a decision only buys a queue of actions/checkout bumps nobody reads.

description: prConcurrentLimit is 0 (unlimited) instead of Renovate's default of 10, and prHourlyLimit is written out at its default of 2 so PR creation is still paced. The default caps how many updates may be open at once, and a manual update only leaves the queue when someone merges it by hand. Once the cap is reached every other update is silently starved: ghcr.io/linuxserver/homeassistant sat two minor releases behind with its bump parked under Rate-Limited on the dependency dashboard, no PR and no notification. branchConcurrentLimit stays unset so it inherits the 0.
